title: Permutations, repeated symbols, and circular orders
terms: permutation count; factorial; ordered selection; arrangement; permutation with repeated symbols; circular permutation.

exposition.text:
An ordered selection of k distinct objects from n has P (n, k) = n!/(n − k)! possibilities. For an
integer n ≥ 1, the factorial is n! = 1 · 2 · · · n, with 0! = 1. Arrangements of a multiset with n total
symbols and multiplicities m , . . . , m number n!/(m ! · · · m !), because exchanging identical

symbols creates no new arrangement.
If n distinct people sit on a circle and rotations count as the same, fixing one person leaves
(n − 1)! orders. Reflections remain distinct unless stated otherwise. Adjacency restrictions can be
handled by treating a required adjacent pair as a block; prohibited adjacency is often counted
by subtraction. Whether positions are labeled changes the count.
When reflections as well as rotations are identified for distinct people, the circular count is
halved for n ≥ 3, because no reflected seating fixes all distinct labels. Relative-order constraints
can instead be handled by symmetry: each ordering of a specified group of k distinct objects
occurs in exactly 1/k! of all permutations.

question.text:
Six distinct people sit around a circular table, with rotations identified but reflections distinct.
Two specified people must not sit next to each other. How many seatings are possible?
(A) 48 (B) 60 (C) 72 (D) 96 (E) 120

solution.text:
There are 5! = 120 total circular arrangements. If the specified pair is adjacent, merge it
into a block: five circular objects give 4! orders, with two internal pair orders, totaling 48.
Subtract to obtain 72.

question.text:
How many permutations of 1, 2, . . . , 7 place 1 before 2 before 3, and also place 4 before 5?
(A) 210 (B) 420 (C) 630 (D) 840 (E) 2520

solution.text:
For any fixed positions occupied by 1, 2, 3, their 3! possible internal relative orders occur
equally often. Independently, the two orders of 4, 5 occur equally often. Exactly one of the
3! · 2! patterns meets both conditions, so the count is 7!/(3!2!) = 420.

question.text:
How many different strings of length five can be made using at most three A symbols, two B
symbols, and one C symbol?
(A) 30 (B) 40 (C) 50 (D) 60 (E) 90

solution.text:
The available multiset has six symbols, so exactly one is unused. Omitting an A leaves
counts (2, 2, 1) and gives 5!/(2!2!) = 30 strings; omitting a B gives 5!/(3!) = 20; omitting C
gives 5!/(3!2!) = 10. The cases have different multiplicities and are disjoint, giving 60.

question.text:
Eight distinct people sit around a circular table. Rotations and reflections count as the same
seating. Two specified people must sit opposite each other. How many seatings are there?
(A) 180 (B) 360 (C) 720 (D) 1440 (E) 2520

solution.text:
Fix one specified person to remove rotational freedom; the opposite seat is then fixed for
the other. The six remaining people can be assigned in 6! ways. Reflection pairs these
arrangements with no fixed arrangement, because all people are distinct and some seats are
exchanged. Dividing by two gives 360.
